- **self**: Guideline 5.2 trademark and IP rules in app metadata (8/3)

## Structure and components

- [statement] Guideline 5.2.4(a) forbids suggesting or implying Apple is a source or supplier of the app or endorses its quality or functionality; 5.2.5 forbids an app that looks confusingly similar to an Apple product, interface (Finder is the named example) or app. A menu-bar utility should avoid Apple-styled branding, icons or wording implying it is a system component. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Guideline 5.2 trademark and IP rules in app metadata · also: https://www.apple.com/legal/intellectual-property/guidelinesfor3rdparties.html
- [statement] Apple's trademark guidelines bar using Apple marks (Apple, Macintosh, iMac, etc.) in whole or in part in a product name. 'Mac' is allowed only if the product is not a computer or OS, is Mac-related, 'Mac' is combined with another non-generic word, and it is not more prominent than the rest of the name. Referential phrases like 'for use with' or 'compatible with' are allowed if the Apple mark is less prominent. The Apple Logo needs a written license. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://www.apple.com/legal/intellectual-property/guidelinesfor3rdparties.html · keywords: Guideline 5.2 trademark and IP rules in app metadata · also: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Guideline 2.3.7 says do not pack metadata with trademarked terms, popular app names, pricing or irrelevant phrases; app names are capped at 30 characters; subtitles must not reference other apps or make unverifiable claims; Apple may modify keywords at any time. Naming competing monitors (e.g. 'like Little Snitch') in keywords or subtitle is a rejection risk. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Guideline 5.2 trademark and IP rules in app metadata · also: https://appreviewready.com/guides/guideline-5-2-legal-rights-review/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Guideline 5.2.1 prohibits protected third-party material such as trademarks, copyrighted works or patented ideas without permission, and misleading, false or copycat representations, names or metadata in the app bundle or developer name; apps must be submitted by the person or legal entity that owns or licenses the rights. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Guideline 5.2 trademark and IP rules in app metadata · also: https://appreviewready.com/guides/guideline-5-2-legal-rights-review/
- [statement] Guideline 4.1(c) forbids using another developer's icon, brand or product name in your app's icon or name without approval. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Guideline 5.2 trademark and IP rules in app metadata · also: https://appreviewready.com/guides/guideline-5-2-legal-rights-review/
- [statement] Apple's 5.2.1 rejection can demand documentary proof of authorization to use a name or control a brand's hardware, or removal of the third-party content from app and metadata. An authorization statement from the developer's own company was accepted in one forum case (anecdotal). (low confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/734904 · keywords: Guideline 5.2 trademark and IP rules in app metadata
- [statement] Guideline 5.2.2 requires that if the app uses, accesses or displays content from a third-party service, the service's terms of use specifically permit it, and Apple asks for authorization on request. A DNS/network monitor that queries third-party reputation or geo-IP APIs or shows their data should keep terms-of-use evidence. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Guideline 5.2 trademark and IP rules in app metadata · also: https://appreviewready.com/guides/guideline-5-2-legal-rights-review/
- [statement] For trademark owners, Apple offers a content dispute form and an App Store name dispute form. Apple usually asks the app owner to resolve it with the complainant, does not itself decide infringement, and resolution can take weeks to months (law-firm commentary, updated 2024-08-27). (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-08-27) — https://harperjames.co.uk/article/protecting-your-apps-trade-mark/ · keywords: Guideline 5.2 trademark and IP rules in app metadata
